Change c0293. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XV.

Context before (unchanged): The servants were gone to a neighbouring fair.

1818 text: All was silent in and around the cottage: it was an excellent opportunity; yet, when I proceeded to execute my plan, my limbs failed me, and I sunk to the ground.

1831 text: All was silent in and around the cottage: it was an excellent opportunity; yet, when I proceeded to execute my plan, my limbs failed me, and I sank to the ground.

Diff: All was silent in and around the cottage: it was an excellent opportunity; yet, when I proceeded to execute my plan, my limbs failed me, and I [-sunk-] {+sank+} to the ground.

Context after (unchanged): Again I rose; and, exerting all the firmness of which I was master, removed the planks which I had placed before my hovel to conceal my retreat.

result.rationale: Replaces the past tense 'sunk' with the standard 'sank' (sink/sank/sunk). Same meaning and event; only a verb-form change in diction, with no interpretive consequence.
